$comment: Projections (ADR 0148; docs/migration-design.md, 'Stages 5 and 6'): what a spelling says, read forwards off its letters by the profile's stated correspondences (sound-read), two spellings compared by sound (sound-compare: same, free, and the places they differ), a word's other spellings of its sound (sound-spellings); and a reading scheme's relation to the spelling it annotates (reading-spells, by dynamic programming), the pieces a script leaves open (reading-variants) and minimal ruby (reading-open). Profiles: es-Latn/standard (Cuban: seseo, yeísmo, b/v, silent h, stress), fa-Arab/standard (ADR 0142's sets); schemes: schluessel (of chg-Arab/standard), tiberian (of hbo-Hebr/tiberian's consonantal text, its points ignored),pinyin and baxter (sets only).

vectors.note: b and v say one sound: a fixed correspondence, so which one is the word's own.
h says nothing: left out, it is a place with nothing on one side.
Two places: the silent h and c before e (seseo).
Seseo: z and s say one sound in Cuba.
c before i says s.
c before a says k, not s: the context decides.
qu before e and k both say k.
c before a and k both say k (kilo).
qu says k only before e or i: before a, q and u are read as themselves.
g before e and j say one sound.
g before a says g.
gu before e is one sound, g.
g before e says the sound of j, not g: the longest match and its context.
gü before i says g and u; gu says g: the diaeresis carries sound.
Yeísmo: ll and y say one sound.
ll is read as one place (the longest written form), not two l.
ch is one sound of its own: not c and a silent h.
y at the end of a word is the vowel i, not the sound of ll.
r at the start of a word is the trill, as rr is.
Between vowels r is the tap and rr the trill: two sounds.
After n, r is the trill.
x says k and s.
Case is folded as the profile folds it.
The accent writes stress: esta is stressed on its first syllable by the default rule, está on its last.
tambien (ends in n) would be stressed on tam-.
háblo says hablo: the default already stresses ha-. The mark is a place of its own (rule stress).
exámen says examen.
A marked monosyllable is stressed; an unmarked one has no stress: tu and tú differ.
An unmarked monosyllable read as itself.
Hiatus: í is a syllable of its own (two syllables); dia would be one.
ú carries the mark, so it does not join a.
Ending in r: stressed on the last syllable by default, as hablár marks.
Ending in n: stressed on the next to last by default; examén is stressed on its last.
ui is one nucleus (two weak vowels).
A silent site is kept; a letter no correspondence names says itself, with no rule.
cui-da-do: ui one syllable; ends in o, so da is stressed.
dí-a: the marked í is a syllable and is stressed.
gu before e is one site; rr one site.
Longest match: ll one site.
One place traded each: the silent h dropped, b for v.
s traded for z (c before a is read back and refused). k, the sound's rare spelling, is never offered for c.
A capital stays a capital.
g before e for j.
gu for g would read as the sound of j; r for rr would be the tap: none.
ll for y, v for b.
s for z (c before o refused); k is never offered for qu.
No stress-mark variants: only b for v; the accent stays.
Final y after a vowel is the vowel: no ll for it.
A word the norm writes with the rare spelling has its leftover: the usual spelling is offered (c before i is read back as s and refused).
The rare spelling is read as the same sound: typed for the usual one it is the right sound with the wrong letter.
A final i is never traded for y: y says i only after a vowel at the end.
y at the end after a consonant is not the vowel.
fa: ص and س say one sound (ADR 0142's sets, fixed).
ذ and ز say one sound.
ط and ت say one sound.
ح and ه say one sound.
ع and ء say one sound.
ق and غ say one sound in Iranian Persian.
س and ش are two sounds.
Vowel marks are left aside: the unmarked spelling says what the marked one says.
Each other letter of the set.
A traded letter keeps its marks.
A letter before a half-space is still that letter.
REVIEW (ADR 0148): Arabizi's e or i, free: i says what e says.
3indi for 3endi: the same sound, an accepted variant.
7 (ḥ) and h are two sounds: no correspondence makes them one.
Only e and i are one: a and e stay apart (enta, inte).
A free correspondence leaves no spelling to learn.
REVIEW (the owner, 2026-11-23): Arabizi's long i written i or ee, free: ee before a consonant is one site and says what e and i say.
akeed for akid: the same sound, an accepted variant (was another sound before the statement).
And the other way round: the course writes meen (who). Sound alone says min is the same; whether min is another lexeme's form is the grader's question (grade/apc-latn/statement-i-ee-another-lexeme).
REVIEW: Arabizi writes no length, so the statement cannot tell a short i from a long one: beent for a short i is a variant too (its known cost).
Only before a consonant: at a word's end ee stays two e's (a final long i is i or e), another sound.
A free correspondence leaves no spelling to learn.
REVIEW (the owner, 2026-11-23): Arabizi's o or u, free: shokran for shukran is the same sound, an accepted variant.
With ou, which the profile's french-ou fold reads as u: mabsot for mabsout is a variant too.
REVIEW: Arabizi writes no length, so a long u written o is taken too (ro7 for ru7, go!), as a short u is (3umr for 3omr): the statement's known cost.
Only o and u: e for u is another sound (re7t is not ru7t by this statement).
REVIEW (the owner, 2026-11-23): a long e written e or ei, free before a consonant: beit for bet.
REVIEW: the statement cannot tell a long e from a short one: beint for bent (a short e) is a variant too, its known cost.
Only before a consonant: at a word's end ei stays e and i, two sounds.
REVIEW (the owner, 2026-11-23): a ق that begins a word written 2 or not: a statement reads no sound out of nothing, so the 2 and the letter after it are one site, 2a or a at a word's start.
abel for 2abel: the same sound, an accepted variant.
2y or y at a word's start (2yes, measure!): the other pair the owner's words need.
REVIEW: the statement cannot tell ق from a word-initial hamza, which the course does not write: 2ana for ana is a variant too, its known cost.
Not before e, i, o or u (free spellings of their own already): 2iza for iza stays another sound.
Only at a word's start: a 2 inside a word is a sound of its own.

REVIEW (the owner, 2026-11-23): the helping vowel in a final cluster, written or not: after a vowel and at a word's end the cluster and the vowel inside it are one site (mr), said once with or without it.
3omor and 3omer for 3omr, ahel for ahl: the same sound, an accepted variant.
Its vowel written as e/i allows: ahil for ahl.
REVIEW: Arabizi writes no length, so a long vowel in that place may be left out too (khams for khamis, Thursday): the statement's known cost.
Not before a final t, which in a verb is the past's -t (I, you) beside its she, -et: kenet (she was) is not kent (I was).
o only where the owner's word has o (3omor, dohor): akol (I eat) is not akl (food).
REVIEW: the vowel marks are left aside.
REVIEW: nothing is stated lost (correspondences: []), so ـه and ـو for -o are two sounds here: accept sets carry بيتو by hand.
No spelling leftover: ص and س are not stated as one sound.
REVIEW: MSA's vowel marks are left aside.
ص and س are two sounds in the standard.
REVIEW: Tajik Cyrillic loses nothing: ҳ and х are two sounds.
REVIEW: Schluessel's transliteration loses nothing: s is another sound than š.
Every piece written by its letter.
A vowel not written; a doubled consonant written once; a final he for a.
An alif that starts a word before vav only carries it: it says nothing.
A half-space says nothing; a capital is read lowercased.
Longest written form: نک for ŋ.

A د for the t of -ta is not stated as a rule (only ṣandūqta is listed, projection/schluessel/spells/listed-ta): not accounted for. (Until the listing, this vector was ṣandūqta صندوقدا; until the statement said پ for b, پز biz: projection/schluessel/spells/pe-for-be.)
A scribe's spelling Schluessel reads otherwise than its letters give is listed word by word, free (the Tadhkira's alif for u); the reading's capital is read lowercased.
A listed word relates before a half-space and a suffix as any word does (the dative -ǧa).
The glossary's spelling is related by the letters, not the listing.
Listed: written with a ye the reading does not give, as Schluessel reads it at its place.
Listed: the locative written with د after q and read -ta, as Schluessel reads it at its place.
Without a spelling a listed word is read as its letters, each traded within its sets: the listing (šahargä written شهریکه) holds for its one spelling.
With its listed spelling the word is one piece no set holds: nothing to trade.
REVIEW (ADR 0148): the course's texts write پ for b (پز biz, پله billä): free, as the scribes' پ, ب for p are.
REVIEW: a double written twice: the second letter is the double's (free), stated before the plain letter's.
And written once.
REVIEW: where پ is written, a card may trade p for b (پ writes b too) and ṗ (ṗ is ف or پ).
A he says a only at the end of a word (or before a half-space).
Without a spelling: each piece traded within every set it belongs to (as the scheme's `variants` traded before ADR 0148).
With its spelling: inside a word an alif writes a, ä or ā, never e, i or u; a final ye writes i, e, ī, ä, à, ē or ā (Mūsā), never a, u or ü.
With its spelling, a vowel the script leaves unwritten is traded for what else it leaves unwritten there (a, ä, e, u, ü), never for a vowel a letter writes (ā, ī, ē).
Minimal ruby with the spelling: the unwritten vowels are open.
A capital is traded for a capital; the silent alif is no place.
Without a spelling: b, a and i are open somewhere (as openLetters read the `variants` before ADR 0148), r and d never.
With a spelling: q, t and its double are closed; a and i open.
Pinyin states each tone of a vowel as unwritten, with the others it may be traded for.
Minimal ruby: the marked vowels, each run of others a dot, spaces kept.
Nothing open: empty.
A scheme without `of` relates no spelling.
x and h trade.
A capital tone letter stays.
The Greek letters do not write a vowel's length: the long α traded for the short one (attic states its lengths as sets, no `of`).
A length with a breathing or an accent on it is traded with them kept, one place at a time.
A capital keeps its case; the circumflex's η and the diphthong are no loss.
Nothing left open: ο is short by its letter.
A scheme without `of` relates no spelling.
Jyutping states no sets (`correspondences: []`): its tones are its `tones`, not traded here.
A logograph's word is listed per logograph: nothing open.
uz-Latn loses nothing: x and h are other sounds in the standard.
Nothing lost, so no other spelling.
йа is я's rare spelling (`rare`): read as the same sound, a fixed place.
е after a vowel says й and е; йе typed there is the same sound.
After a consonant е is е alone: йе there says another sound.
ADR 0148's example: ц at a word's start says с (ц is с's rare spelling there).
A word written the usual way is offered no rare spelling: no йахши.
A word the norm writes with the rare ц is offered its usual spelling (no course word has ц yet).
No Цалом: ц is с's rare spelling at a word's start, never offered for a usual с.
The accent is part of the letter's sound; grading's marks policy decides a mark left out before the sound question (CORRECT_MARKS).
The letters write no length, so none to trade on the writing side: the loss is the attic scheme's.
Fourteen letters, fourteen sounds.
Jyutping writes each sound one way.
Characters list a reading per sign: no sound statement.
The points are passed over (`ignores`): the relation is of the consonantal text. Each consonant its letter, shewa and tsere unwritten, î with its yod.
Unpointed, the same path: a pointed and an unpointed spelling relate alike.
A doubled consonant is one letter (the dagesh is a point); the acute is part of its vowel's piece.
A final â is written with he; a doubled t one tav.
A maqaf-bound word's hyphen is said and not written; a medial kaf before a letter.
ô written without its vav (a defective spelling): free.
ō written with a vav (a full spelling): free.
A medial mem at the end of a word is not this relation's: it stays a slip.
ś is written ש, never ס: another sound in the Tiberian reading.
The divine name is read as its qere: a perpetual qere is stated word by word, the letters as one written form.
After a prefix's vowel the qere loses its first vowel.
The Pentateuch's הוא read hîʾ: the other perpetual qere of the course's texts.
No `loses`: the relation gives reading cards no options to trade.
The same sounds with another stress (ADR 0148: orthographic for the k, phonemic for the unstressed que): the letter place is still named, the stress is no place of the spelling.
Only the stress is another: no letter place.
Another sound.
A capital letter that is dropped leaves its capital to the next letter.
d and t before e and i are soft: deti says ďeťi (Mistrík 14).
v before a voiceless consonant says f.
ch is one letter; l before i is soft; b at the end says p.
Final devoicing: the word's own letter is d.
i and y after b: one sound.
k before a voiced consonant says g.
v after a vowel at the end and u after o at the end both end the diphthong.
ä is e after a labial.
ď before e is the soft d's rare spelling: the same sound.
y keeps t hard, i makes it soft.
A long vowel is another sound.
č and c are two sounds.
d at the end for t.
y for i. ť at the end has no other spelling here: ď and ť are not stated with voicing, so that every d and t before e and i is not offered with a caron.
The soft consonants' carons are rare there, never offered.
A word written with the rare ä offers the usual e.
e after m is the usual spelling: ä is never offered for it.
After k, y is the rule and i rare: a word the norm writes with i offers y.
y after k for i, the rare one: kept, as kasa is for casa; ý after l is not traded (soft l).
One place each: v before š, t before k.
-ov for -ou.
v after a vowel before a consonant is u̯, but u is its spelling only after o at the end.
No ťi: the caron is rare there.
A profile without `sound`: the question is never asked.
-en after a consonant at a word's end says the syllabic n that gessn writes; ss is free with ß.
The falling diphthong ia, and ß: both free spellings.
The 2nd person's -scht at a word's end says what -sch does (Moser has both).
ie is a free spelling of the diphthong ia: wie for wia.
